objective: Preserve a clean, stable person cutout in OBS during gameplay without a physical green screen.
stage: Native OBS filter integrated into app controls; motion acceptance pending

constraints.hardware: Previously observed Ryzen 5 5600H, GTX 1650, about 8 GB RAM
constraints.camera: Previously observed 640x360 at 30 FPS; keep unchanged for first comparison
constraints.privacy: Local recordings and inference only; no uploads or paid API calls

acceptance.criterion: Visibly cleaner hair, face and shoulder boundaries than the original on the same footage, reviewed on dark and light backgrounds.
acceptance.status: RVM silhouettes visually smoother, but no candidate meets the combined quality and timing requirement. No quality percentage established.

acceptance.criterion: Head turns and moving hands remain present, without persistent holes or conspicuous trailing silhouettes; re-entry recovers.
acceptance.status: Head turns and hand/face occlusion captured; exit/re-entry not demonstrated in the clip.

acceptance.criterion: Measure mask responsiveness separately from OBS output FPS; target additional delay below 100 ms, with no sustained delay above 150 ms.
acceptance.status: Native isolated processing improved to ~33 FPS. Physical source-to-OBS bridge delivered 20.6 updates/s with 111 ms median and 140 ms p95 request-to-canvas acknowledgement; physical camera-to-OBS presentation latency remains unmeasured.

acceptance.criterion: No material gameplay regression or sustained OBS rendering overload with Asphalt, voice and watching active.
Restore settings, enabled state, original program scene and virtual-camera state after the experiment; never start streaming or OBS recording.
acceptance.status: Original OBS scene, camera transform, filters and virtual-camera state independently verified intact. Old probe server required assisted closure; corrected socket cleanup passed a separate actual worker/viewer lifecycle test.

nativeIntegration.resourceState: All native workers and probe servers stopped. OBS remains open on the original scene, virtual camera restored; no stream/recording started.
recoveryFindings: Old HTTP keep-alive socket prevented automatic test-server shutdown; assisted closure was required.
An overlapping next test caused a prior final scene readback to fail. The new OS-owned loopback guard covers cleanup too.
Corrected lifecycle explicitly closes owned sockets and stopped in 333 ms with a viewer and idle socket.

verification.existingSuite: 109/110 passed in sandbox; the sole failure was EACCES to a loopback test server. That single protocol test passed with loopback networking allowed.
verification.newChecks: Native worker+server lifecycle, wrong-origin rejection, invalid-path rejection, source-to-OBS alpha agreement, independent OBS restoration audit

nativeIntegration.nextAction: Replace screenshot polling and separate renderer transport with a direct native capture/filter path before production integration. Then test actual Asphalt gameplay and posed movement; do not add more codecs or UI polish.

nativeDirectFilter.architecture: Native C OBS GPU video filter, private ONNX Runtime DirectML, latest-frame worker; no Python, snapshot polling, JPEG, Browser Source or webcam ownership handoff in the active path.

measurements.scope: Native filter attached directly to Webcam; frame age starts at the filter readback, not camera exposure.

nativeDirectFilter.decision: Keep ratio .5. Higher-detail .6 was approximately 10 updates/s with 94 ms processing and was reverted.
nativeDirectFilter.checks: 110/110 regression tests passed; TypeScript/Vite build passed; actual OBS Original/Native adapter and unchanged transform verified.
limits: Processing/frame-age measurements start inside the filter and exclude camera exposure and final display.
Short local webcam probe; no full posed movement, sustained gaming, thermal or voice/watching concurrency acceptance.
Hair fringes and low-quality camera detail remain; no green-screen-equivalence percentage.
Native plugin is a local unsigned prototype, not a release installer.
nativeDirectFilter.activeState: Native filter enabled; legacy owned removal disabled; existing webcam source/IDs/transforms retained.

nativeContinuityFollowup.trigger: User second recording: cutout intermittently disappears to black despite previous sparse screenshots passing.
nativeContinuityFollowup.cause: 250 ms age threshold removed the cutout during processing/capture delays; output-lock cache fix alone did not address this.
changes: Keep cached cutout visible across processing deadlines; report stalled separately.
Capture at most once per OBS video tick.
Honor native stalled status instead of masking it with saved processed-frame counts.
Require fresh output when enabling, including frame counter reset across OBS restarts.

verification.fixture: First eight seconds of previously authorized local webcam clip, looped through temporary OBS media source with identical native filter.
verification.tests: 124-test regression suite passed; expanded 13-test webcam adapter suite passed after final changes, including two new regression cases

diagnosticHistory: First continuous live probe failed startup because a saved frame counter exceeded the restarted worker count; comparison corrected.
Next live capture was all empty: raw webcam inspection confirmed nobody in view, so it cannot assess continuity. Replaced by the saved fixture test.
Earlier virtual-camera capture was in Original mode and was not treated as cutout evidence.
limits: Every fixture output frame checked for missing subject; not a matched replay of the newly supplied recording.
Holding a stale result prevents a blink but can briefly freeze motion; a permanently stalled worker remains a failure.

orderedChanges: Separate input/output locks; input double-buffer and output triple-buffer pointer ownership; consume before waking worker.
Two GPU staging surfaces: map previous tick before submitting current copy; preserve capture timestamp.
Upload output texture only on new output sequence.
Before/after 15-second continuous clip, per-frame disappearance/near-repeat checks, real webcam off/on/off timings and control restoration.
limits: Short matched fixture on one laptop; not gameplay, long-session, or full camera-exposure-to-screen acceptance.
Near-identical images use gray-frame difference threshold .05; still poses and encoder changes affect the proxy.
Old sampled age starts after synchronous readback; new age includes the previous-tick staging interval.
A native diagnostic maximum of 2954 ms was observed during startup/first-inference warmup; steady-state sampled age was 63 ms median and 110 ms p95.
Holding old output during a permanent stall can still freeze it; this change reduces delivery contention rather than removing that explicit recovery limitation.
nativeBufferingPass.currentState: OBS loaded buffered-handoff-v2; normal webcam native filter left enabled; transform unchanged.
